reviewer: /root coordinator; source inspection, not independent reviewer certification
scope: Cross-check shift-by-date financial report against timestamp-ranged daily sales and active business-day assignment. Static only; no full shift/day workflow or provider execution.

assessment.observed_behavior: DailyStatementQueryService.GetAsync(date) computes top-level sales over the Cairo [midnight(date), midnight(date+1)) UTC window. Its shift section selects ShiftEntity.BusinessDate == date, then BuildShiftSummaryAsync aggregates all non-cancelled orders by that shift ID without applying the date window. Shift.Open freezes BusinessDate from Cairo date at opening. CheckoutOrderHandler obtains BusinessDayId from BusinessDayGate.TryGetActiveAsync, which returns any Open/Closing/Reopened day without comparing that day BusinessDate to the current Cairo date.
assessment.conditional_interleaving: If a shift and business day opened on Cairo date D remain open past midnight, and checkout is accepted on D+1 before the prior business day is closed, the order timestamp belongs to D+1 while the order retains the prior active BusinessDayId and ShiftId. The D daily statement can then include that order in a D shift summary but exclude it from D timestamp-ranged top-level sales; the D+1 statement can include it in top-level sales while excluding the D shift from D+1 shift list. Source supports the path, but this exact lifecycle was not executed and actual product policy may expect closure before midnight.
assessment.counterevidence_and_limits: The business-day close evaluator blocks closure while any shift remains open, and the source comments define business date as Cairo calendar date with no late-night rollover. That does not itself prevent the active day and shift from remaining open after midnight, but may indicate an operator-controlled closure expectation. Existing tests cover Cairo timestamp range and day-level reports separately; no cross-midnight open-shift/order scenario was located in the bounded test scan. Existing finding FIN-015 concerns stale shift admission across shift handover and is distinct per the saved business-day candidate; avoid duplicate attribution.
assessment.financial_effect: Potential inconsistency among report sections and day-to-shift reconciliation, not evidence of duplicate/missing persisted ledger postings. The impact is conditional on an open operational day/shift crossing Cairo midnight and on consumers expecting date-partitioned shift rows to reconcile to date-partitioned sales.
assessment.recommendation: First specify the intended boundary invariant: (A) require business day and relevant shift to be closed before Cairo midnight/new date operations, or (B) allow overnight shifts and allocate sales/shift rows by transaction business date rather than shift-open date, or (C) label shift rows as full-shift totals that can cross daily windows. Do not simply add the daily timestamp filter to shift summary without assessing cash reconciliation and late shift close semantics.
required_regression_tests: With fixed Cairo instants, open shift/day on D and submit a valid sale after midnight on D+1 before closure; compare D and D+1 daily statement sales with shift sections and explicit expected policy.
Control case: close shift and business day on D before midnight, open new day/shift on D+1, assert each report section reconciles to its defined cohort.

Test rejection/acceptance and business-day attribution after midnight under whichever owner-approved policy is selected; verify persisted BusinessDayId, ShiftId, date summary and close cash snapshot together.
assessment.execution: No test, endpoint, database query, clock manipulation, or runtime execution performed.

canonical_finding: Not added to MASTER_FINDINGS in this coordinator cross-check; keep as a conditional candidate pending owner policy and independent reviewer challenge. Do not classify as realized accounting loss or runtime-proven defect.
